title: Do we really need the Rademacher complexities?
abstract: arXiv:2502.15118v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We study the fundamental problem of learning with respect to the squared loss in a convex class. In the subgaussian setting, the sharpest known sample complexity bounds are characterised via fixed points associated with the limiting gaussian process. In more general settings (for example, heavier-tailed scenarios) the state-of-the-art bounds rely on localised Rademacher complexities, which are often difficult to control and can be considerably larger than their limiting gaussian counterparts.   We show that if one has access to coarse information on the covariance structure of the underlying class, it is possible to derive an upper bound on the sample complexity that matches the state-of-the-art rates in the gaussian setting---even in heavy-tailed regimes. translated_title: 我们真的需要Rademacher复杂度吗？
translated_abstract: 我们研究了在凸函数类中关于平方损失学习这一基本问题。在次高斯设定下，已知最尖锐的样本复杂度界是由与极限高斯过程相关联的不动点所刻画的。而在更一般的情形下（例如重尾场景），最先进的界依赖于局部化Rademacher复杂度，这类复杂度通常难以控制，且可能远大于其对应的极限高斯复杂度。我们证明，只要能够获得关于底层函数类协方差结构的粗略信息，就可以推导出样本复杂度的上界，该上界在高斯情形下能达到最先进的速率——即使是在重尾情形下同样成立。因此，在相当弱的最小假设下，具有相同L2结构的学习问题——即便是涉及重尾分布的问题——也拥有相同的上界。
tldr: 该论文证明只需利用函数类协方差结构的粗略信息，即可在重尾情形下推导出与高斯情形最先进速率相匹配的样本复杂度上界，从而表明学习问题无需依赖难以控制的局部化Rademacher复杂度。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that coarse information on the covariance structure of a class suffices to derive sample complexity upper bounds matching state-of-the-art Gaussian rates even in heavy-tailed regimes, eliminating the need for hard-to-control localized Rademacher complexities.
